name: Omoide Yokocho
notes: Yakitori under the train tracks, 5 min from the hotel. If you want more than ramen.

name: Ramen Mitaba (Kabukicho, till 5:45am)
notes: Ramen 5 min from the hotel, open till 5:45am. The jet-lag bowl.

name: Imo Pippi (sweet-potato dessert)
notes: Asakusa: crème-brûlée sweet potato, cash only, 11am open (so only if you're still in Asakusa).

name: Iyoshi Cola Asakusa Rokku
notes: Asakusa: craft cola made in front of you. Opens 12:30, so a Nov 30 Kappabashi add-on instead.

name: Koffee Mameya
notes: Omotesando: the best coffee shop in Tokyo, no sign, beans from 20 roasters. 10–6.

name: The Roastery by Nozy Coffee (Cat St)
notes: Cat Street: roastery + espresso martinis. On the walk between Micasadeco and Watchnian.

name: Sedai Coffee & Roasters
notes: Harajuku: tiny roaster, 4.8, cheap. Two min from Micasadeco.

name: The Matcha Tokyo Omotesando
notes: Omotesando: matcha latte with a window over the street. 11–6:50.

name: Menchirashi (carbonara udon)
notes: Harajuku: the carbonara udon. 30-min line, next door to Micasadeco. Only if you skip Onodera.

name: Harry Harajuku Terrace (otter cafe)
notes: Harajuku: the otter café. Reserve. Novelty, skip unless Mom wants the otters.

name: Mega Don Quijote Shibuya
notes: Shibuya: 7 floors of Don Quijote, 24 hrs, tax-free on 7F. Souvenir run any night.

name: The SG Club (Shibuya)
notes: Shibuya: one of the world's top-50 cocktail bars, opens 6. Not on a jet-lag night.

name: Iyoshi Cola Asakusa Rokku
notes: Asakusa: craft cola, 12:30–6:30, a 5-min detour from Kappabashi.

name: American Diner Andra (Ueno)
notes: Ueno: the viral cheeseburger dunked in a skillet of cheese. 11:30–2 lunch, 10 min from Kappabashi. Only if you skipped the market snacks.

name: Bongen Coffee Ginza
notes: Ginza: Japanese-style espresso bar, 30-min line, 10–5.

name: Glitch Coffee Ginza
notes: Ginza: single-origin, 9–6. Coffee nerds' pick; Bongen for the vibe.

name: Ginza Hachigou (6-seat ramen, Bib Gourmand)
notes: Ginza: 6-seat Bib Gourmand ramen with truffle ravioli, reservation only, closed Mon (so not today).

name: Iroriya Higashiginza (irori izakaya)
notes: Higashi-Ginza: basement irori izakaya, ikura bowl, drums when the caviar comes. Dinner alt if T doesn't come through.

name: Katsudon-ya Zuicho
notes: Shibuya: katsudon, 8 seats, one dish. Closed Sun; a lunch alt any other day.

name: Shima (Nihonbashi steak)
notes: Nihonbashi: the other legendary steak (Kobe sirloin, the ¥9,600 takeaway sando). Closed Sun, ~¥30k pp. Backup for T; book via byFood.

name: Wagyumafia The Cutlet Sandwich (Nakameguro)
notes: Nakameguro: the wagyu katsu sando. Same street as T; lunch, not dinner.

name: Bar Zoetrope
notes: Shinjuku: 300 Japanese whiskies, 5 min from the hotel.

name: JB's Tokyo (burgers, Yoyogi)
notes: Yoyogi: the best cheap cheeseburger in Tokyo, 11 seats, 5 min from Shinjuku Station. If you get back early and hungry.

name: Little Nap Coffee Stand (Yoyogi Park)
notes: Yoyogi Park: cortado by the train tracks. Morning-of coffee if you're up early.

name: Hakuichi (gold-leaf ice cream)
notes: Higashi Chaya: the gold-leaf soft serve, ¥900. Do it once.

name: Amano Tea Shop (Higashi Chaya)
notes: Higashi Chaya: tea shop with a tatami room in back; matcha set with a sweet, ~¥1,300.

name: Kanazawa Castle Park
notes: Next to Kenroku-en: the rebuilt white castle, free grounds, 20 min if you want it. (teamLab's castle show was a 2023 one-off; nothing scheduled for Dec 2026.)

name: Turban Curry (Kanazawa curry)
notes: Hirosaka: Kanazawa's thick black curry with a katsu, ¥1,200, 5 min from Kenroku-en. Lunch alt if the market line is long.

name: Gyukatsu Katsugyu Sanjo-Kawaramachi
notes: Across the street from the hotel, B1: gyukatsu (rare beef cutlet you finish on a stone), 4.9 across 4,300 reviews, 10:30am–10:30pm. The any-day lunch.

name: Hikiniku to Come (Gion)
notes: Gion: hamburg steak course grilled over charcoal in front of you, refillable rice. Reserve; closed Wed. Lunch or dinner alt any day but Dec 9.

name: Pontocho Alley
notes: Out the back door: the lantern lane along the river. Walk it tonight on the way home.

name: Tenryu-ji
notes: Arashiyama: the Zen garden, 30 min, if the rickshaw leaves you time before lunch.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
notes: Arashiyama: the grove on foot, 20 min, if you want it without the rickshaw.

name: Gion Komori (warabi mochi)
notes: Gion: warabi mochi on tatami, 11–6:30, cash. Closed Tue, so today, not tomorrow.

name: Mouriya Gion (Kobe beef)
notes: Gion: Kobe beef on the teppan in front of you; the lunch set is the value play. Lunch alt to Gion grazing.

name: Itoh Dining by Nobu (Gion)
notes: Gion: Nobu's Kyoto room, wagyu + black cod miso. Dinner backup if Hyotei can't be had.

name: Takoyaki Wanaka Dotonbori
notes: Dotonbori: the takoyaki line locals stand in. Let them cool 5 min.

name: Chibo Dotonbori (okonomiyaki)
notes: Dotonbori: the okonomiyaki institution, griddled at your counter. If you'd rather sit than stand before Kokuryu, skip the tray.

name: Rikuro's Namba (jiggly cheesecake)
notes: Namba: the jiggly cheesecake, baked in front of you, ¥1,000. Grab one on the walk home; breakfast tomorrow.

name: Bear Paw Cafe (Uehonmachi)
notes: Uehonmachi: a bear's paw hands you your parfait through a hole in the wall. Cute, slow, 15 min from the hotel.

name: The Spa at Four Seasons Osaka
notes: Dojima: the Four Seasons spa, 10 min from Umeda. A massage + ofuro soak instead of the second mall hour, if Mom wants it. Book ahead.

name: Mr. Hiro Car Studio (JDM garage + cafe)
notes: Taisho: a JDM dream garage with a café and simulators, 5.0 across 3,700 reviews. Dad's, if he's a car guy; 25 min from Namba.

name: Universal Studios Japan
notes: If you'd trade the whole Umeda/Yamazaki day: Super Nintendo World + Harry Potter. It's a full day and a 10,000-step crowd. Not worth it for two 50-year-olds who don't game; left here so you can overrule.

name: Katsuo-ji (daruma temple, Minoh)
notes: Minoh: the temple of 10,000 red daruma dolls, 1 hr out by train + bus; pair with Minoh Falls (40-min walk down). The better trade for the Umeda afternoon if you want nature over malls.

name: Myshopper (personal color)
notes: Sinsa: the 16-type personal color analysis, 1 hr, ~$100. Squeeze in before Park Jun if Reberry runs short.

name: Seongsu-dong (alt afternoon)
notes: Seongsu-dong: the Brooklyn of Seoul. Already on tonight's route.

name: Tokyo Tower
notes: Shibakoen: walk under it after dinner, lit till 11. You don't need to go up.

name: Yakiniku Coco Nemaru Ginza
notes: Ginza: wagyu yakiniku in private rooms, 1 min from Ginza Stn. The swap if two sushi counters is one too many.

name: Yoroniku Ebisu
notes: Ebisu: the wagyu yakiniku omakase. Book a month out. Other swap.

name: Shima (Nihonbashi steak)
notes: Nihonbashi: closed Sundays, so not tonight.

name: Mimasu (1910 family sushi, Yotsuya)
notes: Yotsuya: 1910 family sushi, ¥4,500 omakase. Closed Sundays; a cheap lunch any other day.

name: Sushi Punch (Azabujuban)
notes: Azabujuban: omakase 7F, closed Sun. Backup for Sushi Yuu on a different night.

name: BUTTER Biei pancakes (Marunouchi Bldg B1)
notes: Same building, B1: the Biei butter pancakes with a 100 g block of butter churned in the window. The other breakfast.

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
notes: One last market breakfast instead, 15 min away, if you'd rather eat standing up.

name: Yaguchi Book Store (Jimbocho)
notes: Jimbocho: the 3-generation film-and-art bookstore, 10:30 open, 10 min from the hotel. If there's an hour.

name: Good Wood Terrace (jerk chicken)
notes: Caribbean jerk chicken in Shibuya (viral after Kanye). Novelty pick.

name: II II II Coffee (Akasaka, weekdays)
notes: Akasaka: 1-person espresso stand, weekdays 7:30–3:30. Coffee pilgrimage only.

name: Common (Roppongi cafe)
notes: Roppongi: big bright all-day café, matcha latte, breakfast plates.

name: Onibus Coffee Yakumo
notes: Yakumo: the roaster's flagship, banana bread with espresso butter. Out of the way.

name: Marufukuro (Tadao Ando, ex-Nintendo HQ)
notes: Birthday-nights hotel option, Dec 7–9. Tadao Ando inside Nintendo's 1889 HQ. ~$500–700/night.
